Distributed computing

Distributed computing studies systems whose components communicate and coordinate while running on separate networked computers. The components exchange messages to achieve a shared objective without relying on one global clock or one perfectly reliable machine.

Introduction

Important challenges include partial failure, concurrent execution, and network delay. A node can stop responding while the rest of the system continues, so protocols must distinguish failure from a temporarily slow connection using limited evidence.

Common applications include search engines, scientific simulations, replicated databases, and large web services. Designers use redundancy, consensus protocols, and careful partitioning to keep these systems useful as demand and infrastructure change.

Coordination

Coordination algorithms define how participants agree on ordering, ownership, and durable results. Their guarantees depend on explicit assumptions about timing, faults, and the messages that the network may delay or discard.
